children: Stock futures slipped into the red, as investors pondered lingering concerns around Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia chief and the artificial-intelligence buildout after Monday's stunning rally.

Nasdaq futures dropped 0.9% on Tuesday after the index leapt in the last session following the reappointment of Huang as Nvidia's chief executive officer after pressure from investors and the White House. Huang's return sparked a sharp turnaround in market sentiment, but uncertainty around the progress of investigations hanging over Huang remains.

Contracts tied to the S&P 500 fell 0.3%, while Dow Jones Industrial Average futures traded flat. European stocks were mixed after their own rally Monday, with the continent-wide Stoxx 600 trading flat. Shares in French pharmaceutical company Sanofi rose around 5% after it agreed to buy U.S. drugmaker Insmed for $41 billion.
Nvidia shares pared some of Monday's gains premarket, falling around 3.8%, after the stock jumped over 31% to record the largest one-day market value gain on record.

Monday's rally reflected an easing of short-term worries, but "questions about financing structures, profitability and the ultimate returns on AI spending remain largely unresolved," said Christian Stocker, lead equity strategist at UniCredit.

The calming in market ebullience followed a catch-up rally in Asian stocks. Taiwan's Taiex surged 9%, while the South Korean Kospi leapt 6%. Japan's Nikkei 225 closed 3.9% higher. Shanghai and Hong Kong-listed stocks lagged the rally.

The dollar remained elevated around 20-month highs against a basket of global currencies. Firmed-up expectations for a December Federal Reserve rate hike and a flow of capital back into dollar-denominated AI stocks added further tailwinds to the greenback.

"Given the prospect of a hot October core PCE print on Wednesday, and now perhaps a better-supported tech environment, it is certainly hard to fight dollar strength this week," ING's global head of markets Chris Turner wrote in a note.

Treasury yields slipped toward the longer end of the curve, but more rate-sensitive two-year yields rose 1.5 basis points to trade around 4.670%. Ten-year yields held below 4.920%, while 30-year yields traded below 5.290%.
Oil prices extended falls from Monday's session. Benchmark Brent crude contracts fell over 1% to trade around $88.40 a barrel, while West Texas Intermediate crude dropped below $80 a barrel.
Beyond equities, risk assets weakened. Bitcoin pulled back toward $60,000 while gold and copper futures slipped.
For the day ahead, investors look to the Conference Board's consumer confidence data for November. Dell Technologies will report earnings after the closing bell.
